idiom_name: background URLSession upload tasks (the system daemon persists and retries)
implementation_notes: On Apple platforms the forwarder is the system: a URLSession created with URLSessionConfiguration.background(withIdentifier:) hands the request to a background daemon that stores it and retries when connectivity returns - the documentation for waitsForConnectivity notes that background sessions ignore the flag because 'background sessions always wait for connectivity'. The application still persists the payload in an outbox first (a file in the app container or a Core Data row) and deletes it only in the delegate's success callback; for non-HTTP endpoints BGTaskScheduler schedules the drain attempt, and the task must be re-registered for the next cycle. The hand-written forwarder is justified when the payload must be sent immediately inside a live process or the transport is not URLSession-based.
pitfalls: The delegate must be re-attached in application(_:handleEventsForBackgroundURLSession:completionHandler:) after the app is relaunched for the transfer, or completions are lost.
waitsForConnectivity is ignored by background sessions (they always wait) and is unavailable before iOS 11; foreground sessions have to set it explicitly.
isDiscretionary lets the system postpone transfers until favourable conditions, which is wrong for time-critical messages.
The outbox file must not be deleted at enqueue time - only the completion callback's success path proves the server accepted it.
